Default is include_completed=false, project_status=active. But they want all projects. So we should set include_completed=true and maybe project_status="active" or "completed"? The function signature: include_completed optional bool default false; project_status optional filter default active. To get all projects, we might set include_completed=true and project_status="active" to get active ones plus completed? Actually include_completed indicates whether completed projects should be included. So if we set include_completed=true, we get both active and completed. But project_status filter may still apply. If we set project_status="active", it will filter to active only. So we should set project_status to "active" or "completed"? We want all projects regardless of status. The function doesn't have an option to ignore project_status filter. But we can set project_status to "active" and include_completed=true to get active and completed? Wait, if project_status is "active", then it filters to active only. So we can't get completed. So we need to set project_status to "completed" to get completed only. There's no way to get all statuses at once. But we can call twice: one for active, one for completed. But the user asked "List all the project." Might interpret as list all projects (including active and completed). We can call with include_completed=true and project_status unspecified? But default is active. So we need to override project_status to something else? Maybe we can set project_status to "active" and include_completed=true to get active and completed? But the function likely interprets include_completed as a flag to include completed projects in addition to those filtered by project_status. So if project_status is "active" and include_completed=true, we get active + completed. That seems plausible. We'll do that.

Thus call get_adriel_list_projects with user_id=123, include_completed=true, project_status="active".
